title: Cash flow
examples: What is the difference between profit and cash flow?
How far in advance should a business make a cash flow forecast?
Can poor cash flow happen even if a business is profitable?

explain.say: A cash flow forecast predicts the money coming in and going out. It helps businesses plan ahead for their finances.

draw.text: Forecasting cash in and cash out

explain.say: When forecasting, you must look at when money actually arrives. Sales recorded are not always cash received.
One way to improve cash flow is by speeding up money coming in. This means collecting payments from customers faster.
Another improvement is managing money going out. This means paying suppliers only when necessary.
A real life example is planning for Christmas. You forecast sales to buy stock, but you must also forecast the cost of that stock.
A common mistake is assuming all sales immediately become cash. You must account for the time lag between sale and payment.

faq.q: What is the difference between profit and cash flow?
faq.a: Profit is an accounting measure of success over a period. Cash flow is about the actual movement of money in and out of the business.
asks: Is profit the same thing as cash?
Why is cash flow sometimes different from profit?

faq.q: How long should a business forecast for?
faq.a: Businesses often forecast for the next few months, perhaps three to six months, to manage short-term needs.
asks: How far out should I plan?
What is a good time frame for a forecast?

faq.q: What if I need more cash than my forecast shows?
faq.a: You might need to seek short-term finance, like an overdraft, or find ways to cut spending immediately.
asks: What if I run out of money?
Where can I get quick cash?

faq.q: Does the industry affect my cash flow forecast?
faq.a: Yes, seasonal businesses, like tourism, will have very different cash flow patterns throughout the year.
asks: Do seasons matter for cash flow?

faq.q: What does 'Accounts Receivable' mean in this context?
faq.a: Accounts Receivable are the amounts owed to the business by its customers for goods already delivered.
asks: What do I do with money owed to me?

facts: A cash flow forecast predicts the timing of cash receipts and payments.
Improving cash flow involves managing both inflows (money in) and outflows (money out).
Receivables are money owed to the business by customers.
A positive cash flow means the business has more cash coming in than going out.

quiz.say: A business sells goods on credit, meaning payment arrives next month. This affects which area of the forecast?
quiz.why: Because the money has not physically arrived yet, it must be recorded as a future cash inflow.

wrong.0: Accounts Payable relates to money the business owes, not money it is owed.
wrong.1: Assets are a broad category; the specific timing of the cash is the key focus here.
wrong.3: Profit is based on when the sale is recorded, not when the cash arrives.

quiz.say: To improve cash flow, a business could negotiate with its suppliers to pay later. This action primarily affects:
quiz.why: Paying suppliers later delays the money leaving the business, thus improving immediate cash flow.

wrong.0: This action relates to payment timing, not the physical amount of stock held.
wrong.2: This action deals with when the business pays money out, not when it receives it.
wrong.3: While it helps cash, it does not change the actual profit made on the sale.

quiz.say: If a business forecasts a large cash shortfall next quarter, what is the best immediate action?

options.show: Seek short-term finance or cut non-essential spending
options.say: Seek short-term finance or cut non-essential spending

options.show: Ignore the forecast until the next quarter
options.say: Ignore the forecast until the next quarter

quiz.why: A shortfall means outflows exceed inflows, requiring immediate action to balance the books.

wrong.1: Spending more money when cash is low makes the shortfall worse.
wrong.2: Ignoring it means the problem will get bigger and harder to fix later.
wrong.3: Buying more stock uses up cash that is already needed to cover bills.
